claims.claim: §1 ceiling: Poisson P(stale)=24% 'matches 25%'; at 30 lands/h P(land in 4 rounds)≈22%, and the survivors land through the untested statics-only lane; max sustainable ≈ 1/T_gate ≈ 10/h ≈ 255/day for any N.

claims.claim: Per-process CPU sums to only 3.7-4.0 cores at 0% idle, so ~6 cores are kernel time that no surviving process owns (scheduler/IPC over 8k threads, fault handling, interrupts). Seeing it would need sudo powermetrics or spindump.

I calibrated the units first: raw mach ticks × 125/3 matched getrusage exactly (0.300 s); host_processor_info ticks matched 100 Hz × 10 CPUs (3005 vs 3004). Result for one 10 s window: host busy 9.99 cores (user 63% / sys 37%). The top-like survivor-only sum was 4.98 cores; top -l 2 -s 10 -n 3000 in the same window summed to 580%. Reaped children credited to surviving parents added about 3.6 cores, giving 8.73 cores attributed to uid-501 processes. The remaining 1.27 cores roughly matches the root/system daemons that top lists by name (1.40 cores: WindowServer 45%, kernel_task 39%, coreaudiod 24%, syspolicyd 7%, ...). So kernel time that no process owns is about 0, within ±0.15 core. A re-run of the sibling probe /tmp/concurrency-scale/.probe_attrib4.py over 15 s gave 78% of busy attributed and 22% unseen, and the unseen share includes those root daemons. The report's own numbers also rule it out: its 60/40 user/sys split caps total kernel time at ~4 cores, so 6 cores cannot be kernel time. Caveat: load is lower now than at 01:40-02:00 (120-164), but the machine was still at 0% idle with the same fork rate.
claims.corrected: Most of the gap between top's sum and 1000% is the CPU of short-lived processes that exited inside the sampling window. Their parents had reaped them, so the time sits in those parents' child-rusage counters: about 3.6 of 10 cores in this window. The rest is named root daemons. Kernel time with no owner is at most ~0.3 core, and attributing it needs no sudo.

claims.claim: The knee is at about 12-15 sessions. In the current era (since 09-16T21:30Z) P(load>=25) jumps from 0.25 at 10-11 sessions to 0.48-0.61 at 12-15.

The cells are thin: 13 sessions is 9 h from 7 days and 12 sessions is 15 h from 10 days. The published table also leaves out levels that break the knee shape: 8 sessions gives 0.25, the same as 10-11, and 26 sessions gives 0.19 over 8 h, with 14 at 0.36 making the curve non-monotone. A day-cluster bootstrap of P(12-15) minus P(10-11), 2000 resamples over 19 days (/tmp/skeptic-a1/knee_robust.py), gives +0.22 with 95% CI +0.01 to +0.40, which barely excludes zero. Paired tests within the same day on adjacent bands, all eras (/tmp/skeptic-a1/placebo2.py): 9-11 vs 12-14 is 13/21 days (one-sided p 0.19), 10-11 vs 12-13 is 14/20 (p 0.06), and 12-14 vs 15-17 is 20/26 (p 0.005). So the within-day step shows up at about 15, not at 12.

The current-era 'knee at 12' rests on 9-15 h per level and a bootstrap CI (+0.01 to +0.40) that nearly includes zero. Treat it as a rising band from 12 to 15 with no plateau after it, not as a sharp threshold.

claims.claim: Within the same day, burst probability was higher at 12-17 sessions than at 5-11 on 21 of 26 days (sign test p~0.001), which controls for era and for the day's workload.

The binomial p is 0.0012 one-sided and 0.0025 two-sided, so 'p~0.001' is the one-sided value. Split by era I get 12/15 + 9/10; the report says 12/16. The test does not control for workload inside a day: hours with more resident sessions are also hours with more active agents. b-agent-concurrency puts the 2.5/core crossing at a median of 5 actively working agents, so activity is the likelier driver. Placebo comparisons show the same direction at every boundary above 12 (12-14 vs 15-17: 20/26; 12-17 vs 18-24: 22/31) and none below (5-8 vs 9-11: 10/17).
